look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Examine the flower head from both sides. The yellow ray florets have reddish-maroon veins underneath, and the head is cupped by broad overlapping green involucral bracts (phyllaries). Look for a dark maroon disk and soft, often lyrately lobed gray-green basal leaves. Smell may be chocolate-like, especially in the morning, but do not identify from fragrance or yellow rays alone.
taxonomy_notes: POWO accepts Berlandiera lyrata Benth. as a distinct species. Berlandiera incisa is a synonym. Do not automatically fold Berlandiera lyrata var. macrophylla into this card: POWO treats Berlandiera macrophylla as an accepted separate species; check the actual concept.

project_inclusion.notes: Source-pool admission independent of county range; Texas nativity alone is not a three-target-county PASS. Preserve any prior internal range evidence.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial forb with leafy basal growth and ascending flowering stalks; variable low mounding to taller growth.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Leaves alternate, often concentrated near base, softly hairy, gray-green, obovate to spatulate or lyrately lobed; terminal leaf portion often larger than small lower lobes. Inspect the actual plant rather than assume all leaves are deeply divided.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Solitary radiate heads on stalks, usually several yellow ray florets with maroon veins on the lower surface, surrounding a reddish-maroon disk. Broad green overlapping phyllaries form a conspicuous cup below the head.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: At fruiting, distinctive green cup-like head structure persists as rays fall; confirm mature cypsela and associated bracts in a macro view.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Hairy, often longitudinally striped flowering stems; check stem and leaf attachment on live material.

confused_with: Berlandiera texana — may share yellow rays and dark disk; check more strongly clasping stem leaves and detailed head/leaf structures, not scent alone.
Berlandiera pumila — similar chocolate-flower relatives; compare leaf dissection, pubescence, phyllaries and mature fruit with a regional key.
Thelesperma spp. — yellow ray or rayless heads can confuse at a glance; check leaves and green cup-like involucral bracts.
comparisons.key_distinctions: Combine ray underside maroon venation, green cup-like overlapping phyllaries, maroon disk and leaf shape. One yellow head is not enough.
